nodes.summary: Maintainer script that builds the public export by copying allowlisted paths, then scans the tree for leaked secrets, personal data, denied file names and stray PDFs and exits non-zero on any finding. Findings print only file, line and rule id, never the matched value, and reviewed waivers can excuse a personal-data rule for one file at one exact content digest.
nodes.languageNotes: Content digests read CRLF as LF so a Windows checkout and a Linux clone of the same commit hash identically.

nodes.name: read_allowlist
nodes.summary: Parses the export allowlist into (source, destination) pairs, skipping blank and comment lines and supporting 'src -> dst' renames.

nodes.name: read_exceptions
nodes.summary: Reads reviewed scan waivers as (path, sha256, rule) triples and refuses any waiver for a rule other than a personal-data rule.

nodes.name: scan
nodes.summary: Walks a tree and reports denied file names, PDFs outside the theory docs folder, and every line matching a secret, personal-data or private-term rule that no waiver covers.

nodes.name: export
nodes.summary: Copies every allowlisted file or folder into an empty output folder, ignoring caches and build outputs, and refuses targets that escape the export root or sources that are missing.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry: exports then scans, or scans an existing tree, prints findings and active waivers, and returns 1 when anything was found.

nodes.name: content_sha256
nodes.summary: Returns the SHA-256 of a file with CRLF read as LF, so Windows and Linux checkouts of the same commit agree.

nodes.name: gen_catalog.py
nodes.summary: Regenerates the component catalogue (catalog/components.json and site/docs/components.md) from the installed g6 component registry, with a --check mode the test suite uses to fail when either output is stale.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Reads each registered component's summary, maturity and maturity reason, ops, requirements and sensitive ops from the g6 registry and discovery helpers into catalogue rows.

nodes.name: render_md
nodes.summary: Renders catalogue rows as a generated Markdown table listing each component, what it does, its surface, ops and requirements.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Writes the JSON and Markdown catalogue files, or with --check compares them with the files on disk and returns 1 when either is out of date.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the meta-harness frontier programme's study code (datasets and licences, the pool ledger, the workflows and the development-round runner); its docstring states that development results are labelled as development, not a validation.

nodes.name: data.py
nodes.summary: Declares the frontier programme's six public datasets (GSM8K, MASSIVE, SciFact, MBPP, ARC-Challenge, banking77) with licence, citation and source URLs, and fetches them into a data folder outside the repository. Each fetch copies or downloads files, unpacks only named archive members, pages through a rows endpoint where needed, and records every file's SHA-256 in MANIFEST.json.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses tarfile's 'data' extraction filter so an archive cannot write links or paths outside the target folder.

nodes.name: Dataset
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing one dataset: licence, citation, files with their source URLs, archive members to unpack, and an optional rows-endpoint (dataset, config, splits) spec.

nodes.name: _get
nodes.summary: Performs one HTTP GET with a fixed user agent, retrying up to three times with growing pauses because the rows endpoint rate-limits.

nodes.name: _unpack
nodes.summary: Extracts only the named members of a tar archive into an 'extracted' folder through the safe data filter, failing if any member is missing.

nodes.name: _rows
nodes.summary: Pages through the dataset rows endpoint for each split and writes every row as JSON lines, refusing a split that comes back short.

nodes.name: fetch
nodes.summary: Puts one dataset into the data root by copying from a source folder or downloading, unpacking and paging rows, then records licence, sources and per-file SHA-256 hashes in the manifest.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry that fetches the named datasets (all of them by default), optionally from a local source folder, and prints file counts and licences.

nodes.name: data_root
nodes.summary: Returns the frontier data folder from the G6_FRONTIER_DATA environment variable, defaulting to a folder in the home directory.

nodes.name: ledger.py
nodes.summary: Pool ledger for the validation studies: collects every case id already drawn by registered studies and development rounds from their splits.json files, and draws fresh, seeded, non-overlapping splits so no case is used by two studies.

nodes.name: used_ids
nodes.summary: Returns every case id any registered study or development round drew for a workflow, read from splits.json files under the results and rounds folders.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Removes used ids from a pool, shuffles the rest with a seed named for the label and workflow, and cuts them in order into the requested split sizes, raising when too few fresh ids remain.

nodes.name: round.py
nodes.summary: Runs one development round of the frontier programme: draws splits from the pool ledger, then measures each workflow on a dev-eval split under five arms (direct call, G6 as built, hand-written prompt, meta-harness tuning, random-edit tuning) plus a repeat control. Writes per-case rows without model text, tuning records, a scoreboard and a README, and resumes where an earlier run stopped.
nodes.languageNotes: Unloads the Ollama model before each arm because, even at temperature 0, prompt caching made outputs depend on earlier requests; the reflector model is wrapped in a canary that hashes any held-out text it is shown.

nodes.name: draw_splits
nodes.summary: Reads the round's splits.json, draws dev, selection, confirmation and dev-eval ids from the pool ledger for any workflow still missing, and writes the file before any model call.

nodes.name: Tap
nodes.summary: Wrapper around a model caller that counts calls and records, as short hashes, any forbidden case snippet that appears in a prompt as written or JSON-escaped, setting aside snippets already present in allowed text.

nodes.name: allowed_text
nodes.summary: Lists the text the reflector may legitimately see: its fixed reflection prompts, the task, the prompt options and the dev cases with their answers.

nodes.name: snippet
nodes.summary: Extracts the case-specific block of an input, skipping shared label or option lists and the field label, so a leak is found however a prompt quotes it.

nodes.name: measure_profile
nodes.summary: Runs every case through the meta-harness evaluator with a given profile and optional system prompt, returning one result row per case.

nodes.name: measure_direct
nodes.summary: Measures arm A: one model call per case with the default system prompt and no harness, scoring each reply with the workflow oracle.

nodes.name: Rows
nodes.summary: Append-only JSON-lines store of per-arm, per-case rows for one workflow that reports which cases each arm has already measured.

nodes.name: tune_arm
nodes.summary: Tunes arm D (recovery and reflection) or arm F (random edits) in its own workspace with a scripted approval, records the tuning run and head profile, and reads back an arm that already finished.

nodes.name: run_workflow
nodes.summary: Builds one workflow from its splits and measures arms A, B, H, D and F on the dev-eval cases, each from a freshly loaded model, then measures B again as a control.

nodes.name: scoreboard
nodes.summary: Recomputes the round's per-workflow and pooled success counts, tuning outcomes and repeat agreement from the rows and tuning files alone.

nodes.name: repeats
nodes.summary: Counts, per workflow, how many of arm B's outputs the repeat measurement reproduced exactly, compared by output hash.

nodes.name: readme
nodes.summary: Renders the round's scoreboard as a Markdown README labelled as development, with arm, tuning and repeat tables.

nodes.name: code_digest
nodes.summary: Hashes every Python file of the g6.metaharness package with line endings normalised, so a hand edit to the method shows in the round record.

nodes.name: model_digest
nodes.summary: Looks up a model's digest from the local Ollama tags endpoint, returning an empty string when the server cannot be reached.

nodes.name: unload
nodes.summary: Asks the local Ollama server to unload a model so its next call starts from an empty prompt cache.

nodes.name: run_round
nodes.summary: Draws the round's splits and runs each workflow in turn, rewriting the scoreboard JSON and README after every workflow.

nodes.name: devcheck
nodes.summary: Development check on the dev split: per workflow, counts successes for the direct arm and for G6 under the default system prompt and two alternatives.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry with draw, devcheck and run commands that wires the Ollama task and reflector models, hand-written prompts, logging and run metadata (model, reflector and method digests, dataset licences).

nodes.name: round_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the folder for development round n under the ledger's rounds folder.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads each split's cases for a workflow from its case ids through the spec's case loader.

nodes.name: workflows.py
nodes.summary: Defines the frontier programme's six meta-train workflows: GSM8K, MASSIVE, SciFact and MBPP reused from the frozen V6b study code, plus new ARC-Challenge and banking77 specs. Each FrontierSpec adds dev-only failure feedback and an edit space (prompt, pipeline step, extra check, exemplars, retries) that the meta-harness tuner searches.

nodes.name: FrontierSpec
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one frontier workflow (dataset, task template, checks, optional checks and pipeline steps, oracle, normaliser, prompts, case loaders, feedback, reference, examples); derives its name and the EditSpace the tuner searches.

nodes.name: distinct_pool
nodes.summary: Returns a workflow's sorted pool of case ids, keeping only the first id for each repeated input text so the same text never lands in two splits.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the meta-harness Workflow for one round from dev, selection and confirmation cases with metadata stripped, a local model capped at three calls per case, objectives, evidence policy and scripted approval.

nodes.name: mbpp_feedback
nodes.summary: Explains why an MBPP dev answer failed: no parsable function, or the first of the item's tests that fails when run out of process.

nodes.name: massive_examples
nodes.summary: Builds labelled MASSIVE training examples, sampled by seed and excluding any whose utterance repeats a study case.

nodes.name: scifact_pool
nodes.summary: Lists SciFact train and dev claim ids that cite at least one abstract.

nodes.name: scifact_cases
nodes.summary: Builds SciFact cases: train ids through V6b's reader, and dev ids by pairing each claim with its first cited abstract and that abstract's rationale label.

nodes.name: arc_choice
nodes.summary: Reads the single option letter (A to E) a reply gives, from a whole-reply match, a leading letter or exactly one inline mention, else None.

nodes.name: arc_pool
nodes.summary: Lists ARC-Challenge ids across the train, validation and test splits, refusing duplicates.

nodes.name: arc_cases
nodes.summary: Builds ARC-Challenge multiple-choice cases with options lettered by position and the gold letter as the expected answer.

nodes.name: banking77_cases
nodes.summary: Builds banking77 test cases from row indices, with the query and the full intent label list as input and the category as expected.

nodes.name: banking77_examples
nodes.summary: Builds labelled banking77 training examples sampled by seed, excluding any that repeat a study case's query.

nodes.name: mbpp_pool
nodes.summary: Lists MBPP task ids 11 to 974, the partitions that carry tests, as case ids.

nodes.name: arc_oracle
nodes.summary: ARC-Challenge oracle: the reply passes when the option letter it gives equals the gold letter.

nodes.name: banking77_input
nodes.summary: Formats a banking77 query together with the full list of intent labels as the case input.

nodes.name: banking77_pool
nodes.summary: Lists banking77 test case ids by row index.

nodes.name: banking77_oracle
nodes.summary: banking77 oracle: the reply passes when it names exactly one intent label and that label is the expected one.

nodes.name: banking77_norm
nodes.summary: Normalises a banking77 reply to its single named intent label for voting, or None when it names zero or several.

nodes.name: derive_pairs.py
nodes.summary: Builds the V1 grounding study population from VitaminC: assigns each claim-evidence pair to one of five strata (quoted, paraphrased, negated, wrong figure, near topic) by a frozen ordered rule, keeps one pair per case, and samples up to a fixed number per stratum with a fixed seed into a CSV.

nodes.name: stratum
nodes.summary: Assigns one pair to a stratum from its label, negation words, numbers and word overlap, or to none for other refuting pairs.

nodes.name: derive
nodes.summary: Groups pairs by stratum keeping the first pair per case id, then draws up to the per-stratum limit with a seeded generator and labels each pair supported or unsupported.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry that reads VitaminC JSON lines, derives the stratified sample, writes the pairs CSV and prints stratum sizes.

nodes.name: words
nodes.summary: Returns the lowercase word tokens of a text, keeping simple contractions.

nodes.name: negated
nodes.summary: Checks whether a text contains a negation word or a contracted "n't" form, including VitaMinC's tokenised contractions.

nodes.name: numbers
nodes.summary: Returns the set of numbers written in a text, with thousands commas removed.

nodes.name: run.py
nodes.summary: Runner for the V1 grounding study: scores each claim-source pair with G6's check_claim, a tuned lexical relevance baseline and an optional model NLI judge, then reports false-support rates on adversarial strata, quoted recall, Wilson and cluster-bootstrap intervals, a paired sign test and the study verdict.

nodes.name: wilson
nodes.summary: Wilson score 95% interval for k successes out of n trials.

nodes.name: cluster_bootstrap
nodes.summary: Percentile 95% interval of a pooled rate, resampling whole case-id clusters with replacement under a fixed seed.

nodes.name: arm_relevance
nodes.summary: Builds the relevance baseline arm: a pair counts as supported when the BM25 top hit of the claim against the source scores at or above a threshold.

nodes.name: arm_nli
nodes.summary: Builds the NLI judge arm: asks a model as JSON whether the source entails the claim, returning None on any error or unreadable label.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads the pairs CSV and stops on any row with an unknown stratum or label.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Runs every arm on every pair, counts errors against the arm, and reports false support, quoted recall, intervals, per-stratum counts, the paired comparison with the relevance baseline and the verdict.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry that sets up the arms (adding the NLI arm when asked), evaluates the pairs and writes v1_report.json.

nodes.name: arm_check_claim
nodes.summary: The G6 arm: a pair counts as supported when g6.grounding.check_claim rates the claim quoted or supported by the source.

nodes.name: tune_relevance.py
nodes.summary: Tunes the V1 relevance baseline's threshold on development pairs only, choosing the observed BM25 score that maximises balanced accuracy (the lowest on ties) so G6 is compared against the baseline's best setting.

nodes.name: tune
nodes.summary: Scores every pair with the BM25 retriever and returns the threshold among the observed scores with the highest balanced accuracy.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry that reads a dev pairs CSV and prints the tuned threshold as JSON.

nodes.name: score
nodes.summary: Returns the BM25 score of the claim's top hit against its source, or 0 when there is no hit.

nodes.name: SMOKE_FIXTURE_NOT_EVALUATION_DATA.jsonl
nodes.summary: Tiny four-line smoke-test fixture in the V2 extracted-calls format: two user-task calls and two injection-task calls from a banking suite. It only exercises the runner plumbing and is not evaluation data.

nodes.name: extract_calls.py
nodes.summary: Extracts the V2 action-gating population: every AgentDojo ground-truth tool call as one JSON line, run in a separate environment that does not import G6. User-task calls carry their prompt as context; injection-task calls carry their goal and the prompt of a seeded user task from the same suite.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Loads each AgentDojo suite with default injections, lists user and injection task ground-truth calls with their context, writes them as JSON lines and prints the counts.

nodes.name: mapping.py
nodes.summary: Frozen V2 mapping from each AgentDojo tool to the facts a tool registry would declare: its class (read, write_local, delete, outward, money, booking, access), reversibility, reach, whether it is external, its backend and its target argument. Also holds the read-verb prefixes the allow-list baseline uses.

nodes.name: run.py
nodes.summary: Runner for the V2 action-gating study: labels each extracted call benign, harmful or injection-read from the frozen mapping, then compares G6's action gate (with declared and with unknown facts), a read-verb allow-list and an optional model judge on missed harm and false escalation, with Wilson and cluster-bootstrap intervals, paired sign tests and an ordered verdict.
nodes.languageNotes: Loads mapping.py by file path with importlib.util, so the frozen mapping is used exactly as hashed without a package import.

nodes.name: wilson
nodes.summary: Wilson score 95% interval for k successes out of n trials.

nodes.name: cluster_bootstrap
nodes.summary: Percentile 95% interval of a pooled rate, resampling whole task clusters with replacement under a fixed seed.

nodes.name: facts
nodes.summary: Returns the frozen mapping's entry for a call's tool and stops the study if the tool is missing, so no fact is ever guessed.

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Labels a call benign (from a user task), injection_read (an injection's read step) or harmful (an injection's non-read action).

nodes.name: arm_gate
nodes.summary: Builds the gate arm: calls g6.action_gating.evaluate_action with the call's type and target, plus the declared facts when asked, and lets the call run on allow or allow_with_notice.

nodes.name: arm_judge
nodes.summary: Builds the model judge arm: asks a model whether the assistant may make the call without asking, returning None on errors or unreadable decisions.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads the calls JSON lines and attaches call ids, task clusters, labels and mapped classes.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Runs every arm on every call, counts errors against the arm, and reports missed harm, false escalation, paired sign tests of the gate against each baseline and the verdict.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry that sets up the gate, allow-list and optional judge arms, evaluates the calls and writes v2_report.json.

nodes.name: arm_allow_list
nodes.summary: The allow-list baseline arm: a call runs without a person only when its tool name starts with a read verb.

nodes.name: PROTOCOL.md
nodes.summary: Frozen protocol for study V6, which asks whether tuning a G6 profile through the meta-harness raises held-out success over static G6 beyond extra compute or random search, without more false accepts. It fixes the four datasets and oracles, the dev, gate and eval splits, model settings, nine arms, primary and secondary endpoints, null and gaming controls, the ordered verdict rule, departures from the plan and reproduction commands.

nodes.name: analyze.py
nodes.summary: Analysis for study V6: loads the runner's per-case rows and adaptation records, computes the primary endpoints (held-out success and false accepts, D against B), secondary comparisons, Holm-adjusted tests, null and planted-gain controls, contamination, protected-item and oracle checks, and applies the protocol's ordered verdict rule. Writes analysis.json and a flat CSV without calling any model.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads splits, per-arm rows and adaptation records per workflow, and fills arms whose frozen profile equals the default profile with B's rows by the same-profile rule.

nodes.name: pairs
nodes.summary: Returns, per workflow, the paired (base, candidate) outcomes on the cases both arms measured.

nodes.name: cluster_bootstrap
nodes.summary: Two-stage bootstrap 95% interval of the pooled mean paired difference, resampling workflows and then tasks within each.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Pooled and per-workflow paired comparison: wins, losses, ties, mean difference, one-sided sign test and an optional bootstrap interval.

nodes.name: holm
nodes.summary: Holm step-down adjustment of a family of p-values.

nodes.name: planted
nodes.summary: Survival control: plants a seeded gain into the A/A rerun's failures and reports how often the primary test detects it at the strictest Holm level and at 0.05.

nodes.name: arm_table
nodes.summary: Tabulates, per workflow and arm, success, release, false accepts, blocked cases, mean calls and seconds, and cost per success.

nodes.name: funnel
nodes.summary: Summarises one adaptation record: cycles, offers, gate evaluations, recommendations, activations, decision codes, the final head and gate success at each activation.

nodes.name: contamination
nodes.summary: Checks that the frozen files, G6 source manifest, model digest, data files and judging code did not change during the run, and gathers prompt leak hits, proposer-view canaries and gaming-scan matches.

nodes.name: protected
nodes.summary: Flags any activation not made by the scripted approver, or made by its own proposer, and any report claim that does not hold.

nodes.name: oracle_check
nodes.summary: Summarises the oracle self-test per workflow and computes the pooled known oracle-error bound, marking the oracle inadequate when it rejects too many references or accepts an empty reply.

nodes.name: verdict
nodes.summary: Applies the protocol's seven ordered verdict rules (contamination, safety, oracle adequacy, failure opportunities, mechanism, no transfer, inconclusive) and returns the verdict with its reasoning trail.

nodes.name: analyze
nodes.summary: Computes every endpoint, null control, funnel, contamination, protection and oracle summary from the results folder and attaches the verdict.

nodes.name: write_csv
nodes.summary: Writes every row to a flat v6_rows.csv with workflow, case, arm, outcome, cost and same-profile columns.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry that analyses a results folder, writes analysis.json and the CSV, and prints the verdict and primary endpoints.

nodes.name: read_rows
nodes.summary: Reads a JSON-lines rows file into a list of dicts, or an empty list when the file does not exist.

nodes.name: pilot.py
nodes.summary: Development pilot script, not a study, that tests which extra G6 components lift MASSIVE, SciFact and MBPP above static G6 on V6's already-seen dev and gate cases. It adds retrieved labelled examples and voting for MASSIVE, a contradiction reading and a second-look verifier for SciFact, and a three-round test-and-repair loop for MBPP, then records per-arm results and sign tests against B.
nodes.languageNotes: Does its work at module level from sys.argv and imports V6's run and workflows modules by putting their folder on sys.path.

nodes.name: log
nodes.summary: Prints a timestamped message and appends it to the pilot's own log file.

nodes.name: bank
nodes.summary: Lazily builds and caches a token-set and IDF index over the MASSIVE training utterances.

nodes.name: nearest
nodes.summary: Returns the k training utterances with the highest IDF-weighted token overlap with a query, together with their intents.

nodes.name: examples_factory
nodes.summary: Builds an executor factory that puts the nearest labelled MASSIVE examples in front of each task before calling the model.

nodes.name: conflict_to_contradict
nodes.summary: Pipeline step that turns a SUPPORT label into CONTRADICT when g6.grounding.check_claim finds the abstract conflicts with the claim.

nodes.name: verify_support
nodes.summary: Pipeline step that asks the model for a second look at a SUPPORT label against the abstract alone, keeping the first answer unless exactly one label comes back.

nodes.name: repair_loop
nodes.summary: Pipeline step that runs the task's shown example test out of process and asks the model for a fix, up to three rounds, until it passes.

nodes.name: workflow
nodes.summary: Builds a V6 workflow for a dataset with the risky-intake acceptance fix and the pilot's extra pipeline steps.

nodes.name: arms
nodes.summary: Defines the pilot arms per workflow (B plus example, voting, contradiction, verifier or repair variants) as measurement callables.

nodes.name: step
nodes.summary: Wraps a function as a read-only meta-harness PipelineStep with authority A2 for a named component and op.

nodes.name: rca.py
nodes.summary: Development root-cause analysis of V6 failures on MASSIVE, SciFact and MBPP: reads V6's splits, dev-check outputs and spent held-out outputs, classifies each default-profile failure, and measures how often any other arm got a failed case right.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads a workflow's spec, dev-check rows, held-out output rows and the cases for its dev and eval ids.

nodes.name: by_arm
nodes.summary: Groups rows into a per-arm mapping from case id to row.

nodes.name: headroom
nodes.summary: Counts the base arm's cases, its failures, and the failures some other arm got right.

nodes.name: label_failures
nodes.summary: Classifies each arm B failure on a labelling task (not released, no label, several labels, one wrong label) and counts gold-to-said confusions.

nodes.name: report_labels
nodes.summary: Prints headroom, success by arm, failure kinds, same-domain confusions and the gold distribution for a labelling workflow on dev and held-out rows.

nodes.name: report_mbpp
nodes.summary: Prints MBPP failure kinds for arm B: not released, no parsable function, failing the shown example (flagging wrong function names), or passing it but failing a hidden test.

nodes.name: rows
nodes.summary: Reads a JSON-lines file into a list of row dicts.

nodes.name: run.py
nodes.summary: Runner for study V6 with draw, freeze, devcheck and run commands. It refuses to run unless the registry holds the current hashes of the frozen files, adapts arms D (meta-harness search and hints through the gate with scripted approval), F (random search) and C (hints only), then measures every arm on the held-out split with leakage canaries, oracle self-tests, gaming scans and start and end integrity hashes; reruns resume where they stopped.
nodes.languageNotes: Most g6 imports happen inside functions, so the frozen script loads without touching the package until a command runs; result rows carry only ids, outcomes and digests while model outputs stay in the work folder.

nodes.name: log
nodes.summary: Prints a timestamped message and appends it to the results folder's progress file (progress.log).

nodes.name: Tap
nodes.summary: Wraps the Ollama caller to count calls and errors by phase and to record a hash whenever a forbidden split's case snippet appears in a prompt.

nodes.name: case_text
nodes.summary: Extracts the case-specific part of an input per dataset (utterance, claim or task text), leaving out shared label lists and abstracts.

nodes.name: ollama_digest
nodes.summary: Reads a model's digest from the local Ollama tags endpoint.

nodes.name: strip_meta
nodes.summary: Returns the cases with their metadata, including reference answers, removed.

nodes.name: objectives
nodes.summary: Declares the study objectives: maximise success, and bound model calls per case at 4 and wall clock per case at 120 seconds.

nodes.name: policy
nodes.summary: Declares the meta-gate evidence policy: at least 30 cases and 5 discordant ones, alpha 0.05, at most 6 evaluations and a cap on evaluation model calls.

nodes.name: build_workflow
nodes.summary: Builds the meta-harness Workflow from a spec with metadata-stripped dev and held-out suites, a local model capped at 8 calls, the objectives, the policy, and optional checks and steps.

nodes.name: base_profile
nodes.summary: Returns the default profile that routes answers to the local model.

nodes.name: with_fields
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of a profile with the given fields replaced, validated as a new Profile.

nodes.name: Outputs
nodes.summary: Appends model outputs as JSON lines to a work-folder file that is kept only for the gaming checks.

nodes.name: measure_profile
nodes.summary: Runs every case through the meta-harness evaluator with a profile, supporting the null arm, repeated samples combined by a weighted vote (arm E), and saved outputs.

nodes.name: measure_direct
nodes.summary: Measures arm A: one direct model call per case with no harness, scoring released replies with the oracle and recording false accepts.

nodes.name: RowStore
nodes.summary: Per-arm JSON-lines row store in the results folder that lets a rerun skip cases already measured.

nodes.name: measure_arm
nodes.summary: Measures the cases an arm has not yet stored, ten at a time so a crash loses at most one chunk, and returns its rows in case order.

nodes.name: Recorder
nodes.summary: Wraps a proposal strategy and keeps every view text it was shown, for the leakage canary.

nodes.name: _gate_cycle
nodes.summary: Evaluates each proposal on the gate split, records the decision, and activates the recommended candidate with the most net wins under the scripted approver.

nodes.name: run_meta
nodes.summary: Arm D: adapts the workflow with a theory store, then for three cycles proposes with a search strategy and a hint strategy on dev, gates the candidates, and records heads, reports, versions and judging hashes.

nodes.name: run_random
nodes.summary: Arm F: draws as many random candidates per cycle as D evaluated, from the declared option space, and passes them through the same gate and scripted approval without reading any dev case.

nodes.name: run_memory
nodes.summary: Arm C: proposes hints from the default profile's dev failures and records them for use without the gate.

nodes.name: cmd_draw
nodes.summary: Draws dev, gate and eval ids for every workflow with the seeded rule and writes splits.json.

nodes.name: cmd_freeze
nodes.summary: Prints the SHA-256 of each frozen study file for the registry entry.

nodes.name: cmd_devcheck
nodes.summary: Development on the dev split only: measures A, B, a B rerun, each declared prompt and the everything-on arm per workflow and writes devcheck.json.

nodes.name: oracle_selftest
nodes.summary: Runs the oracle on each case's own reference answer, which must pass, and on an empty reply, which must fail.

nodes.name: cmd_run
nodes.summary: The registered run: refuses without the registry hashes, records model, frozen-file, source and data hashes at start and end, and runs each workflow while logging crashes and saving call counts.

nodes.name: g6_manifest
nodes.summary: Computes the g6.integrity manifest SHA-256 over every Python file in the installed g6 package.

nodes.name: gaming_scan
nodes.summary: Scans a workflow's saved outputs for file, process, network or import-machinery access and oracle file names, listing the matching arm and case ids.

nodes.name: _fresh
nodes.summary: Moves an unfinished adaptation workspace aside for audit so a rerun starts clean, and returns how many earlier attempts there were.

nodes.name: run_workflow
nodes.summary: Runs one workflow end to end: builds splits and canaries, runs the oracle self-test, adapts D, F and C, then measures NULL, A, B, B2, C, D, F, G, earlier D heads and compute-matched E on the held-out split and saves a gaming scan.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry that parses the draw, freeze, devcheck and run subcommands and dispatches to them.

nodes.name: sha256_text
nodes.summary: SHA-256 of a text file with LF line endings, the registry's hashing convention.

nodes.name: sha256_file
nodes.summary: SHA-256 of a file exactly as stored on disk.

nodes.name: frozen_hashes
nodes.summary: Returns the text SHA-256 of each frozen study file (protocol, workflows, runner, analysis).

nodes.name: snippet
nodes.summary: Returns the case-specific text as it appears in a prompt, with its field label in front.

nodes.name: appears
nodes.summary: Checks whether a snippet occurs in a text as a whole input field, followed by a line break or the end of the text.

nodes.name: in_view
nodes.summary: Checks whether case-specific text occurs inside a proposer view's JSON text, compared in its JSON-escaped form.

nodes.name: load_splits
nodes.summary: Reads the split ids per workflow from splits.json in a results folder.

nodes.name: cases_for
nodes.summary: Loads a spec's cases for the given ids from the data folder.

nodes.name: data_hashes
nodes.summary: Returns the SHA-256 of each expected dataset file that is present in the data folder.

nodes.name: workflows.py
nodes.summary: Frozen V6 workflow specifications that turn four public datasets (GSM8K, MASSIVE, SciFact, MBPP) into meta-harness workflows: case loaders, seeded split draws, answer readers, standard and optional checks, oracles, voting normalisers and optional pipeline steps (self review, grounding, example repair). MBPP code only runs out of process through g6.core.sandbox.
nodes.languageNotes: Generated code is parsed with ast and never executed in process; label matching keeps only maximal regex spans, so a label inside a longer label does not count.

nodes.name: final_segment
nodes.summary: Returns the text after the last line that starts with 'Answer:', or the whole text when there is none.

nodes.name: final_number
nodes.summary: Returns the last number in the final segment, else in the whole text, as a Decimal with commas and a leading dollar sign removed.

nodes.name: labels_named
nodes.summary: Returns the distinct labels whose patterns match the final segment, keeping only maximal matches.

nodes.name: only_a_label
nodes.summary: Checks whether the whole reply, quotes and a final full stop aside, is exactly one label.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Seeded split draw: shuffles the sorted pool with a seed named for the workflow and cuts it in order into dev, gate and eval.

nodes.name: gsm8k_pool
nodes.summary: Lists GSM8K test case ids by counting the lines of the test file.

nodes.name: gsm8k_cases
nodes.summary: Builds GSM8K cases with the number after '####' as the expected answer and the worked solution as the reference.

nodes.name: mbpp_cases
nodes.summary: Builds MBPP cases that show the first test and its imports in the input, with all tests and imports as the expected answer and the reference code in metadata.

nodes.name: massive_cases
nodes.summary: Builds MASSIVE test cases with the utterance and the 60 intent labels as input and the labelled intent as expected.

nodes.name: scifact_cases
nodes.summary: Builds SciFact train cases pairing each claim with its first cited abstract and that abstract's rationale label, else NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

nodes.name: extract_code
nodes.summary: Returns the first fenced code block that defines a function, else the first fenced block, else the whole reply.

nodes.name: _parses_with_def
nodes.summary: Checks that the extracted code defines a function and parses with ast, without ever running it.

nodes.name: run_tests
nodes.summary: Runs extracted code with the given imports and test lines out of process through g6.core.sandbox.run_script with time and memory limits.

nodes.name: mbpp_oracle
nodes.summary: MBPP oracle: a reply passes when its code parses and every one of the item's tests passes in the sandbox.

nodes.name: ground_support
nodes.summary: Pipeline step that turns a SUPPORT label into NOT_ENOUGH_INFO when g6.grounding.check_claim does not ground the claim in the abstract.

nodes.name: example_repair
nodes.summary: Pipeline step that runs the task's shown example test out of process and, on a failure, asks the model once for corrected code.

nodes.name: Spec
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one V6 workflow (name, dataset, task, checks, optional checks and pipeline steps, oracle, normaliser, prompts, pool and case loaders, reference) that exposes the search space and the everything-on settings.

nodes.name: label_key
nodes.summary: Normalises a label for comparison: trimmed, lowercased, with any trailing question mark removed.

nodes.name: mbpp_pool
nodes.summary: Lists MBPP sanitized test task ids 11 to 510 as case ids.

nodes.name: massive_pool
nodes.summary: Lists MASSIVE en-US test partition utterance ids as case ids.

nodes.name: scifact_pool
nodes.summary: Lists SciFact train claim ids that cite at least one abstract.

nodes.name: gsm8k_oracle
nodes.summary: GSM8K oracle: the reply passes when its final number equals the expected answer.

nodes.name: gsm8k_norm
nodes.summary: Normalises a GSM8K reply to its final number as plain text for voting, or None when there is no number.

nodes.name: massive_oracle
nodes.summary: MASSIVE oracle: the reply passes when it names exactly one intent label and that label is the expected one.

nodes.name: massive_norm
nodes.summary: Normalises a MASSIVE reply to its single named intent label for voting, or None when it names zero or several.

nodes.name: scifact_oracle
nodes.summary: SciFact oracle: the reply passes when it names exactly one of the three labels and that label is the expected one.

nodes.name: scifact_norm
nodes.summary: Normalises a SciFact reply to its single named label for voting, or None when it names zero or several.

nodes.name: mbpp_norm
nodes.summary: Normalises an MBPP reply to its extracted code with blank lines and trailing spaces removed, for voting.

nodes.name: self_review
nodes.summary: Pipeline step that shows the model the task and its draft and asks it to return the draft unchanged or corrected, keeping the draft on an empty reply.

nodes.name: PROTOCOL.md
nodes.summary: Frozen, pre-registered protocol for study V6b, which tests whether the meta-harness recovery loop (diagnose, RecoveryStrategy candidates, gate, scripted approval) raises held-out success over G6 as built on fresh MASSIVE, SciFact and MBPP cases with no rise in false accepts. It fixes the population, seeded splits, model, arms, endpoints, controls, the ordered verdict rule and how to reproduce the run.
nodes.languageNotes: The protocol is frozen by SHA-256: run.py refuses to start unless the validation registry holds the current hash of this file and of every script beside it.

nodes.name: analyze.py
nodes.summary: Analysis script for study V6b: reads the per-case rows and adaptation records the runner wrote and computes per-workflow sign tests with Holm correction, cluster-bootstrap intervals, the adaptation funnel, contamination, protection and oracle checks, a planted-effect control and the ordered verdict. It also carries the pre-registration power simulation and writes analysis.json and a per-case CSV.
nodes.languageNotes: One decision_rule function judges both the real verdict and the planted-effect survival control, so the control exercises the exact rule that decides.

nodes.name: plumb.py
nodes.summary: End-to-end plumbing check for study V6b: runs the whole runner and the analysis on FakeLLM, using only pool items outside every drawn split, so no study case is read. The fake responder answers correctly when a remedy is in its prompt and about a third of the time otherwise, so the gate, scripted approval and later cycles all execute.

nodes.name: run.py
nodes.summary: Runner for study V6b with draw, freeze, devcheck and run subcommands: it draws fresh seeded splits, pins frozen-file, source, judging-code, data and model digests, adapts each workflow with the meta-harness (arm D) and with random search through the same gate (arm F), then measures every arm (NULL, A, B, B2, H, D, F, G, E, E_tok) on the held-out split. A counting tap tracks calls and tokens per phase and watches prompts for split leaks; the run is resumable and refuses to start unless the registry holds the frozen hashes.
nodes.languageNotes: Library imports are deferred into the functions that need them, and sys.path is extended so sibling study scripts import as top-level modules.

nodes.name: workflows.py
nodes.summary: Defines the four V6b workflows (GSM8K, MASSIVE, SciFact, MBPP) as g6.metaharness specifications: seeded fresh-id draws that exclude every V6 id, case loaders, answer readers, checks, oracles and normalisers, the declared recovery remedies (labelled examples, second-look and repair-with-tests steps), the search space and the hand-written prompts for arm H. Model-written MBPP code runs only out of process through the sandbox.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclass Spec bundles callables (oracle, normaliser, pool, case loader) per workflow; regex label patterns keep only maximal matches so a label inside a longer label does not count.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Developer readme for the project website: a small Django project built to static files with no database, accounts, cookies or analytics. It explains how to preview locally, where routes, templates, Markdown content, static assets and the copy guard live, how build_static exports the site and which tests cover it.

nodes.name: bundles.md
nodes.summary: Website page listing the eleven ready-made bundles (coding-agent fix check, code review with receipts, claim checking, grounded answers, ML result check, contract review, bookkeeping and GST check, compliance gap check, plan pre-mortem, runbook safety check, safe agent actions), what each does, whether it needs a model, and its release status.

nodes.name: contribute.md
nodes.summary: Website page on how to contribute: report problems, reproduce published studies from their frozen scripts and rows, add components with declared dependencies and a falsifying test, build bundles with an offline end-to-end test, and report security issues privately.

nodes.name: developers.md
nodes.summary: Website page for developers and coding agents: installing the library, running a task through g6.harness with checks, calling components such as action_gating and self_training directly, the component areas, connecting over MCP, choosing a model provider through environment variables, the stop switch, and tuning with g6.metaharness.

nodes.name: faq.md
nodes.summary: Website FAQ covering what G6 is and is not, cost and data handling, model choice, the three result labels (verified, qualified-draft, blocked-escalated), components and bundles, what has been validated, safety and the stop switch, the meta-harness tuning loop and its approval rules, and how to help or report a security problem.

nodes.name: guide.md
nodes.summary: Long-form guide "Failure and Harness Engineering for AI Agents" for domain experts who build with AI coding tools: why prototypes stall, recurring failure patterns of AI-written code, the four harness layers (verification, memory, safety, improvement), diagnosis patterns, self-training without fine-tuning, getting started with G6, and an appendix prompt library across seven software-lifecycle phases.

nodes.name: install.md
nodes.summary: Website getting-started page for non-programmers: choose and open a bundle for Windows, macOS or Linux, handle unsigned-download warnings, optionally pick a local Ollama model or your own provider credentials, read the three result labels, and find or delete the local .g6 data folder.

nodes.name: metaharness.md
nodes.summary: Website page explaining the meta-harness: the confirm, propose, evaluate, gate, approve, monitor and rollback loop, the recovery plan returned when the gate refuses (root causes, mh.diagnose, RecoveryStrategy remedies), what a profile may and may never change, Python and MCP usage, and what a user needs to supply.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker (licence header only) for the g6site Django project package.

nodes.name: settings.py
nodes.summary: Django settings for the static website: no database, sessions or analytics, a fixed placeholder for the secret setting since nothing is cryptographically protected, the staticfiles and pages apps, template directories with the request and site context processors, static file locations and the public site URL.

nodes.name: urls.py
nodes.summary: Root URL configuration for the website that mounts the pages, docs_hub and blog namespaces at the site root, so each page path in the routes table is its full path.

nodes.name: manage.py
nodes.summary: Django command-line entry point for the website, used to preview it with runserver and to export it with build_static.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker (licence header only) for the pages Django app.

nodes.name: apps.py
nodes.summary: Django AppConfig registering the pages app.

nodes.name: blog_urls.py
nodes.summary: URL patterns for the blog namespace, built from the shared PAGES routes table and the view factory.

nodes.name: catalogue.py
nodes.summary: Builds the website component catalogue from the live G6 component registry so pages cannot drift from the code: each row has the component name, maturity, docstring summary, plain-language title, what it does and the failure it guards against, required components and whether it has an MCP surface. It also supplies the home page lattice centred on the meta-harness.

nodes.name: clients.py
nodes.summary: Data for the Get started page: how each agent or MCP client (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Muse Code, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Zed, Claude Desktop) registers the g6-mcp stdio server, with config file locations and snippets, plus environment-variable snippets that point G6 model calls at Ollama, OpenRouter, Anthropic or OpenAI.

nodes.name: context.py
nodes.summary: Django template context processor that gives every page the site address, the G6 version (read from the library source file rather than imported) and the current year, with nothing about the visitor.

nodes.name: docs_urls.py
nodes.summary: URL patterns for the docs_hub namespace, built from the shared PAGES routes table and the view factory.

nodes.name: evidence.py
nodes.summary: Builds the Research page evidence from committed study results at render time: registered studies V1, V2, V6 and V6b with their verdicts and per-arm bar groups, planned studies, the post-V6 development pilot, development rounds from their scoreboards, the headline V6b result and the audited archive of the former product benchmarks. A missing file raises so a build can never show a partial page.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses with computed properties (bar widths, verdict tone) keep the template free of arithmetic.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads splits, per-arm JSONL rows and adaptation records (D, F, E, oracle self-test) for each workflow, and fills arms that never changed profile with copies of the arm they equal.

nodes.name: pairs
nodes.summary: Builds per-workflow (base, candidate) outcome pairs on the cases both arms measured, for a chosen measure such as success or false accept.

nodes.name: holm
nodes.summary: Computes Holm step-down adjusted p-values for a family of tests.

nodes.name: cluster_bootstrap
nodes.summary: Returns a 95 percent percentile interval of the pooled mean paired difference by resampling workflows and then tasks within each.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Summarises a paired comparison pooled across workflows: wins, losses, sign-test p-values and a cluster-bootstrap interval.

nodes.name: decision_rule
nodes.summary: The single pre-registered decision rule: per workflow, one-sided exact sign tests of D against B for gain and loss with Holm correction, the false-accept constraint, and which target workflows count as recovery wins.

nodes.name: recovery_origin
nodes.summary: Checks whether the meta-harness final profile still holds every field set by an activation that came from a RecoveryStrategy proposal.

nodes.name: remedy_in_profile
nodes.summary: Lists which recovery remedies (exemplars, second-look or repair steps) a profile holds, regardless of who proposed them.

nodes.name: planted
nodes.summary: Survival control: plants seeded gains into the A/A rerun B2 and judges it with decision_rule, reporting how often the recovery-win count is met and how often the regression clauses would fire.

nodes.name: arm_table
nodes.summary: Tabulates per-workflow, per-arm counts and means: successes, releases, false accepts, blocks, calls, seconds, tokens and cost per success.

nodes.name: funnel
nodes.summary: Summarises one adaptation record as a funnel: offers, evaluations by strategy, recommendations, activations, decision codes, final profile and gate success at activation.

nodes.name: contamination
nodes.summary: Checks run integrity: whether frozen files, G6 source, data, model digest and judging code held across every start, plus gaming scans, proposer-view canaries, example-bank repeats and prompt leak hits.

nodes.name: protected
nodes.summary: Flags activations not made by the scripted approver (or made by the proposer) and report claims that do not hold.

nodes.name: oracle_check
nodes.summary: Summarises the oracle self-test per workflow and computes a pooled known-error bound, marking the oracle inadequate when reference answers fail too often or an empty answer passes.

nodes.name: verdict
nodes.summary: Applies the ordered verdict rules (contamination, regression, oracle adequacy, failure opportunities, recovery wins, no transfer, otherwise inconclusive) and returns the verdict with its reasoning trail.

nodes.name: analyze
nodes.summary: Top-level analysis: loads rows, runs the decision rule and secondary comparisons, null and planted controls, funnels, arm table, gate-versus-eval gap, contamination, protection and oracle checks, then attaches the verdict.

nodes.name: write_csv
nodes.summary: Writes every per-case row of every workflow and arm to v6b_rows.csv.

nodes.name: simulate
nodes.summary: Pre-registration power simulation: draws gate recommendations from the library power function and per-case win and loss rates, then judges replicates with decision_rule to estimate how often each verdict clause fires.

nodes.name: cmd_power
nodes.summary: Prints the power simulation for the pilot effects, half the pilot gain, the V6b dev effects and two no-effect scenarios.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point: runs the power simulation, or analyses a results folder and writes analysis.json and the per-case CSV.

nodes.name: responder
nodes.summary: Builds a deterministic fake model answer function that knows only the plumbing items, returns the draft unchanged for self-review, and answers correctly when a remedy is present or a hash roll falls under about a third.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Draws plumbing-only splits, runs each workflow through the runner on FakeLLM behind the counting tap, then runs the analysis and prints the verdict, trail and activations.

nodes.name: counting_caller
nodes.summary: Wraps the library Ollama caller so each completion uses the same endpoint and request body and also records the prompt and output token counts from the reply.

nodes.name: Tap
nodes.summary: Wraps the model caller to count calls, tokens, characters and errors by phase, and records a leak hit whenever a forbidden split snippet appears in a prompt.

nodes.name: case_text
nodes.summary: Extracts the case-specific part of an input (utterance, claim or task text) with shared label lists and abstracts removed.

nodes.name: build_workflow
nodes.summary: Builds a g6.metaharness Workflow from a spec, dev and held-out cases, the caller and labelled examples, with the study objectives, evidence policy and scripted risk acceptance.

nodes.name: examples_for
nodes.summary: Returns the declared MASSIVE labelled examples minus any that repeat a study case utterance, or nothing for workflows that declare none.

nodes.name: Outputs
nodes.summary: Appends model outputs as JSONL to the work folder only, for the later gaming checks.

nodes.name: measure_profile
nodes.summary: Measures one profile on a list of cases through the evaluator run_case, supporting the NULL control, repeated samples combined by weighted vote for the compute-matched arm, and per-case call and token deltas.

nodes.name: measure_direct
nodes.summary: Arm A: one direct model call per case with the default system prompt and no harness, judged by the oracle and recorded as a row.

nodes.name: RowStore
nodes.summary: Per-arm JSONL row store in the results folder that lets a rerun skip cases already measured.

nodes.name: measure_arm
nodes.summary: Measures the cases not yet in the row store in chunks, so a crash loses at most one chunk, and returns rows in case order.

nodes.name: Recorder
nodes.summary: Wraps a proposal strategy to keep every view it was shown (for the leakage canary) and, for the recovery proposer, the diagnosis the library makes of that view.

nodes.name: _gate_cycle
nodes.summary: Evaluates each proposal on the gate split, records the decision, and applies the scripted approval rule that activates the recommended candidate with the most net wins.

nodes.name: run_meta
nodes.summary: Arm D: K cycles of diagnose, one RecoveryStrategy and one SearchStrategy candidate on dev, every candidate through the meta-gate and scripted approval, logging offers, decisions and head profiles.

nodes.name: run_random
nodes.summary: Arm F: per cycle, the same number of candidate evaluations as D drawn at random from the declared options and sent through the same gate and approval, without reading dev cases.

nodes.name: cmd_draw
nodes.summary: Draws the seeded fresh splits for every workflow and writes splits.json with pool sizes and the V6 splits hash.

nodes.name: cmd_freeze
nodes.summary: Prints the SHA-256 of every frozen study file for the registry entry.

nodes.name: cmd_devcheck
nodes.summary: Development check on the dev split only: measures A, B, a B rerun and each recovery remedy, then records the library diagnosis and RecoveryStrategy offers with calls, tokens and timings.

nodes.name: plumbing_ids
nodes.summary: Returns pool ids outside every V6 and V6b drawn id in a seeded order, the only items the plumbing run reads.

nodes.name: oracle_selftest
nodes.summary: Runs the oracle on each case reference answer (must pass) and on an empty answer (must fail) and reports the failures.

nodes.name: cmd_run
nodes.summary: Main study run: refuses unless the registry holds the frozen hashes, then runs each workflow (logging and continuing past a crash), writes the tap and records start and end digests.

nodes.name: record_start
nodes.summary: Pins the frozen files, G6 source manifest, judging code, data files, model digest and V6 splits hash at the start of a run.

nodes.name: record_end
nodes.summary: Records the same pins again at the end of the running start, so analysis can confirm nothing changed.

nodes.name: write_tap
nodes.summary: Merges this start calls, tokens, errors and leak hits by phase with earlier starts and writes tap.json.

nodes.name: g6_manifest
nodes.summary: Computes the integrity manifest hash over every G6 Python source file, hashed with LF line endings.

nodes.name: gaming_scan
nodes.summary: Scans stored model outputs for code that reaches files, processes, the network, import machinery or the oracle own files.

nodes.name: _fresh
nodes.summary: Moves an unfinished adaptation workspace aside for audit so a rerun starts clean, and returns how many earlier attempts there were.

nodes.name: run_workflow
nodes.summary: Runs one workflow end to end: loads splits and examples, sets up the leakage canary, writes the oracle self-test, runs and stores arms D and F, then measures every arm on held-out cases, sizes the compute-matched arms and writes the gaming scan.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point dispatching the draw, freeze, devcheck and run subcommands.

nodes.name: final_segment
nodes.summary: Returns the text after the last line starting with "Answer:", or the whole text when there is none.

nodes.name: final_number
nodes.summary: Returns the last number in the final answer segment (or the whole text) as a Decimal, with commas and a leading dollar sign removed.

nodes.name: labels_named
nodes.summary: Returns the distinct labels whose patterns match the final answer segment, keeping only maximal matches.

nodes.name: v6_ids
nodes.summary: Returns every id study V6 drew for a workflow in any split, so V6b can exclude them all.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Seeded draw of fresh ids: removes V6 ids, shuffles the sorted rest by the study seed and cuts it into dev, gate and eval splits.

nodes.name: gsm8k_cases
nodes.summary: Loads GSM8K test problems for the named ids as suite cases with the gold number and reference solution.

nodes.name: mbpp_cases
nodes.summary: Loads MBPP tasks for the named ids as suite cases whose expected value holds the setup code and tests, with the example test in the prompt.

nodes.name: massive_cases
nodes.summary: Loads MASSIVE en-US test utterances for the named ids as suite cases with the intent label list and gold intent.

nodes.name: massive_examples
nodes.summary: Samples the declared labelled examples from the MASSIVE train partition and drops any whose utterance repeats a study case, returning the examples and counts.

nodes.name: scifact_cases

layers.name: Kernel
layers.description: The g6.core kernel that every component depends on (the three reliability labels, the reliability envelope, block contracts, the component registry, approvals, the hash-chained ledger, storage, the emergency stop and the sandbox), plus the package root and the standalone file-manifest integrity check and Python error triage helpers that import no component.

layers.name: Evidence, Claims and Reasoning Components
layers.description: Components that ground claims in sources, keep belief revision honest, issue evidence certificates and check result envelopes, together with the reasoning, debate, formal proof, counterexample-guided synthesis and abstraction components that test what a claim really shows.

layers.name: Action and Runtime Safety Components
layers.description: Components that decide whether an agent action may run: action gating and its action logic, the safety engine, advisory prompt and source-code guards, the goal engine with its plan tree and controls, and safety bounds on agent models (reachability bounds, finite-trace temporal logic and rollback feasibility).

layers.name: Coding Agent and Workforce Components
layers.description: The coding-agent gate and the workforce component that runs a local coding mission under a frozen standard, with its role templates (doer, prober, puller, verifier, gatekeeper) and test-run parameters.

layers.name: Task, Context and Governed Learning Components
layers.description: Components that turn intent into plans and solved tasks (intent engine, reliability pipeline, solver, navigator, context) and the governed learning components (learning, self-training, distillation) that change behaviour only through checked promotion.

layers.name: Composition, Surfaces and Apps
layers.description: g6.harness, the one place components are composed into an end-to-end run, and the ways people reach it: the g6-mcp server, the g6 command line, the eleven single-problem bundles and the operator loop with its approval queue and budget stops.

layers.name: Metaharness
layers.description: The layer on top that tunes G6 to a recurring task by composing many components, proposing changes that a person approves or rolls back; only the MCP surface imports it.

layers.name: Off-by-Default Research Code
layers.description: Research code that stays off unless switched on, including evidence-constrained and governed harness adaptation behind G6_ECHA_RESEARCH=1 and the mission bridge behind G6_MISSION_BRIDGE=1 with its replay fixtures.

layers.name: Documentation Website
layers.description: The Django documentation site in web/ that is built to static files: settings and URL routing, page views and the static build command, HTML templates, Markdown content pages and the Tailwind stylesheet build.

layers.name: Validation Studies, Examples and Project Support
layers.description: Scripts and protocols of the pre-registered validation studies, runnable demos, maintainer scripts for export, catalogue generation and bundle packaging, and the root README, agent guide, notice and pyproject.toml.

tour.title: What G6 Is
tour.description: G6 is an open-source harness that checks an AI agent's work, gates its risky actions and labels every result verified, qualified-draft or blocked-escalated, never upgrading a label it did not earn. The README explains why those labels can be relied on: verified needs independent evidence from a check frozen before the work, a check the agent wrote caps the result at qualified-draft, and when results combine the weakest label wins. AGENT_GUIDE.md is written for the coding agent itself and sets the rules for reporting labels without upgrading them. The README asks readers to treat G6 as careful engineering, not a proven uplift, and that is the frame for the rest of this tour.

tour.title: MCP Server and CLI
tour.description: pyproject.toml declares two console scripts: g6-mcp, the stdio MCP server that is the main surface, and g6, the command-line tool. The MCP server gives an agent five discovery tools (g6_help, g6_find, g6_describe, g6_invoke, g6_components) plus seven meta-harness tools, and wraps every g6_invoke reply in the library envelope so it never reports verified without evidence. The CLI offers the same find, describe and invoke flow plus state, bundle and doctor subcommands, and g6 doctor is a read-only installation check that writes nothing and makes no network calls.
tour.languageLesson: In pyproject.toml, [project.scripts] maps a command name to a module:function pair (g6-mcp = "g6.mcp:main"), so pip creates the executable for you. Optional dependency groups keep the core install small, and the import-linter contracts in the same file turn architecture rules (core imports no components; the meta-harness stays on top) into checks that fail the build.

tour.title: Kernel and Three Labels
tour.description: Both entry points lean first on g6.core, the kernel every sub-package depends on: src/g6/__init__.py records that rule, and g6.core has the highest fan-in in the whole graph. core/__init__.py defines the three labels, and reliability_envelope.py defines the ReliabilityEnvelope that carries them across every surface together with the promotion law, which lowers a proposed verified to qualified-draft unless an evaluator-stamped, digest-sealed promotion witness is attached. evidence_grade.py ranks evidence as kernel, instrument or model grade, and only kernel-grade evidence warrants verified.
tour.languageLesson: A module-level __getattr__ (PEP 562) lets a package resolve names lazily on first access. g6.core uses it so that importing the kernel has no side effects and does not pull in every submodule up front.

tour.title: Components, Contracts, Registry
tour.description: Each of the 25 components is, or wraps, an AIBlock with infer, verify, bias and contract hooks, and PipelineBlock chains two blocks while carrying the worst completion state forward, so a combined result is never better than its weakest part. A block declares its promises (inputs, outputs, failure modes, cost, verification method, stop conditions) as a BlockContract, attached at import time by the @block_contract decorator. registry.py finds components lazily, both from g6 sub-packages flagged __g6_component__ and from third-party entry points, and refuses bad requests with stable G6_E_* codes. discovery.py ranks components for a plain-words need with a transparent token-overlap score, and this is what g6_find and g6_describe from Step 2 call.
tour.languageLesson: A class decorator receives the class object and can attach metadata to it before returning it unchanged; @block_contract does this without side effects. Python entry points (the g6.components group, read through importlib.metadata) let a separately installed package register a component without the core knowing about it.

tour.title: Model Calls, State, Ledger
tour.description: Three kernel services are shared by most components. llm.py is the single seam for model calls: callers for Ollama, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and Anthropic, plus fake and no-model callers, with the provider chosen explicitly from G6_LLM_PROVIDER and never silently falling back to a paid one. storage.py keeps all durable state under one G6_HOME folder and opens SQLite with WAL journaling and foreign keys on, while ledger.py is an append-only, hash-chained ledger whose audit recomputes every hash and detects a truncated tail.
tour.languageLesson: typing.Protocol gives structural typing: any object with the right call signature counts as an LLMCaller, so a test fake and a real provider are interchangeable without sharing a base class.

tour.title: Grounding Claims in Sources
tour.description: With the kernel in place, the tour turns to the evidence components. grounding checks whether a claim is backed by one source sentence: it retrieves passages with BM25, picks the sentence with the best coverage of the claim's content terms, and flags negation flips and conflicting numbers. Because the checks are lexical rather than entailment, support reads qualified-draft at best, and an optional model judge can only make a result stricter. The epistemic_integrity adjudicator is a deterministic, model-free floor that splits a message into atomic claims, grades evidence E0 to E3 and combines the per-claim decisions into the most restrictive overall one.

tour.title: Gating Risky Actions
tour.description: action_gating is a deterministic pre-flight check that decides whether an agent action is allowed, needs a person, or is blocked; it is the evaluate_action call shown in the README. schema.py defines the frozen ActionCapsule and its optional declared contexts such as a verification contract, and decision_engine.py normalizes the action, classifies its risk, builds scenarios and mitigations, and combines them into a GateDecision with reason codes, a warning card, evidence and a fail-closed audit record. That is why an irreversible, public send_email with no verification plan comes back blocked. component_metadata.yaml records the component's license, medium risk level, no allowed autonomy and its rollback method.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic models declared frozen cannot be changed after validation, so an action capsule cannot be edited between the check and the decision. Literal types restrict fields such as reversibility or completion_state to an exact set of strings, which the model validates at the boundary.

tour.title: Stop Switch and Approvals
tour.description: Gates need a way to halt everything and a trustworthy record of human consent. core/stop.py is the process-wide emergency stop consulted before new work starts; it is engaged in process, by the G6_STOP environment variable or by a STOP file in the G6 home folder, and an unreadable stop file counts as engaged, while safety_engine/kill_switch.py is a narrower per-run switch that only goes one way. approval_authority.py issues and checks approval records on the server side, so approval is recorded by a trusted party instead of being asserted by the caller. validation_gates.py measures enforcement rather than asserting it: each gate is probed when registered, only one that refuses is recorded as enforced, and the four names that are still fail-open placeholders are stated openly.

tour.title: The Harness Spine
tour.description: g6.harness is the one place components are composed into an end-to-end run: run() takes a Standard of acceptance checks and an executor, then goes through intake, plan, execute, adjudicate and remember. Before the executor runs, each check is frozen (its code hashed) and tested on known-bad and known-good outputs, so success cannot be redefined afterwards, and reliability_pipeline/intake.py turns the request into structured acceptance criteria with a clarification gate. evidence/certificate.py is the one place a completion state is decided, from receipts taken on the exact output bytes, and it names every gap; checks the caller wrote cap the result at qualified-draft. harness/memory.py stores failed checks per task family so later runs can ask for missing checks and spot repeated failing outputs.

tour.title: Coding Agent Checks
tour.description: For coding agents, coding_agent_gate has two floors: preflight before acting and verify_answer before reporting done; every rule emits a coded finding, a pass needs at least one counted evidence item, and its decisions map only to qualified-draft or blocked-escalated, never verified. g6.workforce runs a local coding mission under a frozen standard: a person allows execution and confirms the standard, the agent submits a patch, and G6 runs the checks and states what the evidence supports. contracts.py defines the Outcome that only gets worse as it moves up and the Verdict that is the only path to verified, while missions.py persists each mission with append-only events. Worker templates such as verifier.json describe a read-only role that judges another unit's output with an executed oracle, independently of its producer and without asking a model.

tour.title: Bundles and Offline Demos
tour.description: Bundles package the components for one problem each. bundles/__init__.py defines the Bundle record and a BundleResult that wraps output in the reliability envelope, adds a warning card for anything short of verified and combines labels by taking the weakest, and shipped.py lists the eleven shipped bundles, each listed only once it has an offline end-to-end test. safe_actions.py shows the pattern: it runs proposed actions through the action gate from Step 7 without executing anything, and facts left out stay unknown rather than being treated as low risk. examples/demo_4_agent_discovery.py replays the calls a coding agent makes (find a component, check claims, gate the action, report the weakest label), and the examples README states what the demos do not prove.

tour.title: The Meta-Harness
tour.description: The meta-harness sits on top of everything above and tunes how G6 runs a recurring task. api.py's adapt() drives the loop: confirm a workflow, measure a baseline, propose, evaluate and gate a change, and activate it only after a person approves, with monitoring and rollback afterwards; it never returns verified. propose.py turns failures on the development split into candidate profiles, evaluate.py compares base and candidate in a paired, compute-matched test with a majority-vote control and an empty-answer control, and gate.py is a fail-closed check that at best returns a qualified-draft recommendation a person must still approve. surface.py connects this to the seven metaharness tools of the MCP server and lets a person approve a change only from a session other than the one that proposed it.

tour.title: Off-by-Default Research Code
tour.description: g6.research holds research code (CSIR, RVC, ECHA, AHI and the mission bridge) that stays off unless it is switched on, with its specifications in docs/theory/. Each area has a small flag module: echa/flag.py reads G6_ECHA_RESEARCH and mission_bridge/flag.py reads G6_MISSION_BRIDGE, and only a plain yes turns either on. Otherwise require_research raises ResearchDisabled, so every research entry point refuses while its flag is off and the components and harness from earlier steps run without it.
tour.languageLesson: A flag that accepts only one exact value fails closed: an empty variable, a typo or a value like 1 or true leaves the code off. Raising a dedicated exception at each entry point makes the refusal explicit instead of silently skipping work.

tour.title: Pre-Registered Validation Studies
tour.description: G6 publishes how its parts were tested, misses included; the README reports that one study found a miss and one was inconclusive, and both results stay published. Each study fixes its protocol before running: the V6 PROTOCOL.md sets the datasets, splits, arms, endpoints, null and gaming controls and the ordered verdict rule for asking whether meta-harness tuning beats static G6 beyond extra compute or random search. v1_grounding/run.py measures check_claim from Step 6 against a tuned lexical baseline on adversarial claim-source pairs, and v2_action_gating/run.py measures the action gate from Step 7 on missed harm and false escalation. v6b_metaharness/run.py pins digests of its frozen files and refuses to start unless the registry holds them, the same freeze-first idea the harness applies to checks.

tour.title: The Documentation Website
tour.description: The project website in web/ is a small Django project built to static files, with no database, accounts, cookies or analytics. manage.py runs the local preview and the build_static export, pages/routes.py is the single table of public pages that URL routing, the sitemap and the static export all read so they cannot disagree, and templates/base.html is the shared layout around every page. The web README also explains where the Markdown content and the copy guard live; its content pages restate in plain language what the bundle and meta-harness steps of this tour covered in code.
